headline: 30 injured as madrasa students clash with police in Brahmanbaria
summary: The clash erupted over loud music played during a police cultural programme, leading to injuries for both students and police personnel.
details: At least 30 people, including madrasa students and police personnel, were injured in a clash at the police lines in Brahmanbaria last night.
The incident occurred around 11:30 PM after a cultural programme organised by the district police to mark the visit of Chattogram Range DIG Abdul Quddus Chowdhury.
Students of Jamia Darul Arkam Al-Islamia Madrasa reportedly asked organisers to lower the volume of the music, as they had examinations the following morning.
The situation escalated when students entered the police lines; police used batons to disperse them, while students allegedly threw bricks and stones.
The injured were taken to Brahmanbaria 250-bed General Hospital and other local hospitals for treatment.
Brahmanbaria SP Shah Mohammad Abdur Rouf held an emergency meeting with Maulana Sajidur Rahman, founder of the madrasa and secretary general of Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh.
Student representatives demanded a written pledge against future music programmes at the police lines, an apology from the SP, and compensation for the injured.
SP Abdur Rouf described the incident as a misunderstanding and stated that CCTV footage would be reviewed to take action against those responsible.
caption:
A dispute over loud music during a police event leads to a violent clash in Brahmanbaria, leaving 30 injured.

Students of Jamia Darul Arkam Al-Islamia Madrasa reportedly asked organisers to lower the volume of the music, as they had examinations the following morning.

The situation escalated when students entered the police lines; police used batons to disperse them, while students allegedly threw bricks and stones.

The injured were taken to Brahmanbaria 250-bed General Hospital and other local hospitals for treatment.

Brahmanbaria SP Shah Mohammad Abdur Rouf held an emergency meeting with Maulana Sajidur Rahman, founder of the madrasa and secretary general of Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh.

Student representatives demanded a written pledge against future music programmes at the police lines, an apology from the SP, and compensation for the injured.

SP Abdur Rouf described the incident as a misunderstanding and stated that CCTV footage would be reviewed to take action against those responsible.

headline: 9 dead in Kolkata hotel fire, 5 victims are Bangladeshis
summary: A journalist and three family members from Kushtia are among those killed in the blaze that broke out at a hotel in Kolkata.
details: A devastating fire at a hotel in Kolkata has claimed the lives of nine people, including five Bangladeshis, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and local police.
The victims include a journalist and three members of a single family from Kushtia, highlighting the personal toll of the tragedy.
Emergency services rushed to the scene to battle the blaze, while survivors described the harrowing experience of seeing death up close.
This incident follows another hotel fire in West Bengal over the last two days, where eight people were reported dead in a separate event.
The Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs is monitoring the situation as the identities of the Bangladeshi victims are confirmed.
caption:
9 people killed in a Kolkata hotel fire, including 5 Bangladeshis.

A devastating fire at a hotel in Kolkata has claimed the lives of nine people, including five Bangladeshis, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and local police.

The victims include a journalist and three members of a single family from Kushtia, highlighting the personal toll of the tragedy.

Emergency services rushed to the scene to battle the blaze, while survivors described the harrowing experience of seeing death up close.

This incident follows another hotel fire in West Bengal over the last two days, where eight people were reported dead in a separate event.

The Bangladesh Ministry of Foreign Affairs is monitoring the situation as the identities of the Bangladeshi victims are confirmed.
